questions.stem: What does the abbreviation CDC stand for in data processing?
options: Central Data Catalogue
Change Data Capture
Continuous Data Copy
Controlled Data Consumption
Common Data Contract
questions.explanation: CDC stands for Change Data Capture: the moment data changes in the database, only the changed data is picked up and pushed to the next layer.

questions.stem: What are the three steps of a CDC framework?
options: CDC Extraction, CDC Processing/Consumption and CDC Serving
CDC Design, CDC Build and CDC Test
CDC Backup, CDC Restore and CDC Archive
CDC Landing, CDC Staging and CDC Reporting
CDC Encryption, CDC Masking and CDC Sharing
questions.explanation: A CDC framework consists of CDC Extraction, CDC Processing/Consumption and CDC Serving; extracting changed data is only the first step.

questions.stem: Which three kinds of change does Change Data Capture pick up?
options: Schema changes, index changes and permission changes
Backups, restores and migrations
A new row added, an existing row updated, and a previously added row deleted
Queries, reports and dashboards
Compression, encryption and archiving
questions.explanation: Changed data can be a new row added, an existing row updated, or a previously added row deleted or dropped.

questions.stem: During CDC Extraction, what does the tag D on a row instruct the ETL process to do?
options: Load a brand-new row into the data model
Duplicate the row into an archive table
Update the row's enter_date only
Close the row previously entered in the data model
Skip the row entirely
questions.explanation: D stands for Delete: when an existing row arrives with tag D, the ETL process must close the row entered previously in the data model.

questions.stem: Why is a CDC process mostly not run in real time?
options: Because databases cannot detect changes quickly enough
Because regulators forbid real-time data movement
Because dashboards only refresh once a day
Because BI teams prefer stale data
Because real-time CDC needs a lot of memory processing, which comes with a heavy TCO, so it depends on ROI
questions.explanation: Real-time plus CDC needs a lot of memory processing, which comes with a heavy total cost of ownership, so the decision depends on the ROI of the business case.

questions.stem: In a CDC framework, which mechanism is used during CDC Processing to load changed data into a Bill Inmon or Ralph Kimball model?
options: One of the three Slowly Changing Dimension types, SCD1, SCD2 or SCD3
A full truncate and reload of every table
A NoSQL document store
A spreadsheet macro
Manual data entry by the BI team
questions.explanation: While loading into any data model, one must load using one of the three Slowly Changing Dimension types, SCD1, SCD2 or SCD3.

questions.stem: Which additional columns typically accompany SCD-enabled tables in a CDC framework?
options: user_name, password and email
enter_date, update_date and end_date, and sometimes a status column with Active or Inactive
latitude, longitude and altitude
currency, exchange_rate and tax
file_name, file_size and checksum
questions.explanation: SCD-enabled tables carry additional date columns, enter_date, update_date and end_date, and sometimes a status column with the values Active or Inactive.

questions.stem: In CDC Serving without a status column, how does a BI team identify new records?
options: Pull rows with all three date columns filled
Pull rows with an empty enter_date
Pull rows with a filled enter_date and empty update_date and end_date columns
Pull rows with a filled end_date only
Pull every row regardless of dates
questions.explanation: To view new records, the BI team pulls rows with a filled enter_date and empty update and end columns; updated rows have enter and update filled, deleted rows have all three filled.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT true of Change Data Capture as described?
options: Only the changed data is picked up and pushed to the next layer
Each extracted row carries an I, U or D tag
Many tools can extract CDC data from a database
Extracting changed data alone is enough to present data on dashboards
CDC Extraction is the first step of the CDC framework
questions.explanation: Extracting only changed data is not the end; two more steps, processing and serving, must be completed before changed data is considered useful.

questions.stem: What does the tag I signal in CDC Extraction?
options: That the row is invalid and should be rejected
That the row should be indexed for faster search
That the row is isolated from other transactions
That the row is an intermediate result
That a new row has arrived and the ETL should load a new row in the data model
questions.explanation: I stands for Insert: when a new row comes it carries the tag I so that the ETL loads a new row in the data model.
